title: One GPU, one price
prompt: SAMPLE: the GPU is $1/hr and you charge $40/mo. How many paying users cover one box?
hints: Turn hourly into monthly first. The ×720 shortcut.
Then users = monthly cost ÷ price. Cancel a zero if both sides have one.
cheat: Hourly ×720 → $720/mo. Users = 720 ÷ 40 = 18. 40 is the price, 720 is the monthly box, 24 is hours in a day — none of those is the user count.

title: Funnel vs ads
prompt: SAMPLE: 10,000 visitors, about 5% convert. Ads plus tools are $3,000 and price is $50. After conversion, how many customers do you have versus the 60 you need to break even? Surplus customers?
hints: 1% of 10,000 is two places left. Scale that to 5%.
Break-even users = 3,000 ÷ 50. Surplus is converted customers minus that.
cheat: 1% of 10k = 100, so 5% = 500 customers. Break-even = 3,000 ÷ 50 = 60. Surplus = 500 − 60 = 440. 500 is the funnel, 60 is the floor, 4,400 added a stray zero.

title: Chunk, then ×12
prompt: SAMPLE: 35% of $2,000 is this month’s fee. What is that as a yearly number?
hints: Build 35% with 10% chips: three tenths plus 5%.
Yearly is monthly ×12, not ×10.
cheat: 10% of 2,000 = 200, three times = 600, plus 5% = 100 → $700/mo. ×12 = $8,400/year. 700 is still monthly. 2,400 is 12×200 (only 10%). 24,000 glued a zero.

title: Swap, then undo a tip
prompt: SAMPLE: 14% of 50 dollars is the 20% tip on a bill. What was the bill?
hints: Swap: 14% of 50 is 50% of 14.
That tip is 20% of the bill. 20% is ×2 then one place left — undo it: ×5, or ×10 then half.
cheat: Swap: 50% of 14 = 7. The tip is $7, which is 20% of the bill, so bill = 7 × 5 = $35. 7 is the tip, not the bill. 70 doubled instead of ×5.

title: Loaded hire, shorter runway
prompt: SAMPLE: $120k in the bank, $20k burn. A hire at $60k salary, loaded ×1.3, billed monthly. About how many months of runway after the hire?
hints: Loaded cost is salary ×1.3, then ÷12 for a monthly add to burn.
New runway = cash ÷ new monthly burn.
cheat: Loaded = 60 × 1.3 = $78k/year → $6.5k/mo. New burn = 20 + 6.5 = $26.5k. 120 ÷ 26.5 ≈ 4.5 months. 6 is the old runway. 78 is the yearly loaded dollars.

title: Growth table, then MRR
prompt: SAMPLE: 100 users at 20%/mo, they charge $20/mo. They claim 50,000 users in a year. Using the 20% table, about what monthly revenue should you smell after 12 months?
hints: 20%/mo is about 9× in a year, not 50×. Start at 100 users.
MRR is paying users × price. Do not treat the 50k claim as real.
cheat: Table: 100 × ~9 = 900 users. 900 × $20 = $18,000 MRR. $1M is 50k × $20 (the false claim). 900 is headcount, not dollars. 2,400 is 120 × 20 (a 20% year, not 20% per month).

title: Take, then processing
prompt: SAMPLE: $2M GMV, 15% take, then about 3% processing on the GMV. Net after fees?
hints: Revenue is GMV × take, not GMV. 10% + 5%.
Fees smell as 3% of GMV, then subtract from take.
cheat: Take: 10% of 2M = 200k, plus 5% = 100k → $300k. Fees: 3% of 2M = $60k. Net 300 − 60 = $240k. 300k is gross take. 2M is GMV.

title: Percent sold, then a slice
prompt: SAMPLE: pre $8M, raise $2M. You can reach 1,000 of 200k buyers at $600/year. What percent did you sell, and what ARR is that slice in thousands? Pick the pair.
hints: Post = pre + cash. Percent sold = cash ÷ post.
The $120M is TAM (200k × $600). The slice is 1,000 buyers × $600.
cheat: Post = 8 + 2 = $10M, 2/10 = 20% sold. Slice ARR = 1,000 × 600 = $600k. $120M is the whole TAM, not the slice. 25% would be cash ÷ pre.

title: Hear 7×8, then park zeros
prompt: SAMPLE: you already know 7×8=56. What is 700 × 8?
hints: Keep the 56 chord. Do not long-multiply 700×8.
700 has two extra zeros versus 7, so the product gets two zeros.
cheat: 7×8=56, two extra zeros → 5,600. 560 is only one zero (70×8). 56 is the chord with none. 4,900 is 700×7.

title: Monthly box, daily quote
prompt: SAMPLE: a GPU is $1/hr. What daily burn should you quote?
hints: Hourly ×720 is monthly. $1/hr → $720/mo.
Daily is monthly ÷30, not ÷365.
cheat: ×720 → $720/mo. 720÷30 = $24/day. 720 is still monthly. 30 is the divisor, not the dollars. 365 treats it as a year of hours.

title: Markup, then heads to cover
prompt: SAMPLE: cost is $16 a unit and you price at 5× cost. Fixed cost this month is $2,400. How many units cover it?
hints: Price is cost × the multiple. 5× on $16.
Units = fixed cost ÷ price, not ÷ cost.
cheat: Price = 16 × 5 = $80. Units = 2,400 ÷ 80 = 30. 150 divided by the $16 cost instead of the price. 80 is the price, not a count. 480 divided by the 5× multiple.

title: Drop zeros, then ×12
prompt: SAMPLE: 30% of $40 is this month’s fee. Yearly?
hints: Tens of percent of tens of dollars: drop zeros, 3×4.
Yearly is ×12, not ×10.
cheat: 3×4=12 dollars this month. 12×12=$144/year. 12 is still monthly. 120 is ×10. 1,440 glued a zero onto 144.

title: Rule of 72 vs a third
prompt: SAMPLE: 6% growth. About how many years to double, and what is a third of that span?

choices.label: 12 years to double, 4 years for a third
12 years to double, 36 years for a third
16.7 years to double, 5.6 years for a third
6 years to double, 2 years for a third

hints: Years to double ≈ 72 ÷ rate.
A third of that span is ÷3, not ×3.
cheat: 72 ÷ 6 = 12 years to double, and a third of 12 is 4. 36 multiplied by 3 instead of dividing. 16.7 used 100 ÷ 6, which ignores compounding. 6 years confused the rate with the doubling time.

title: Ceiling months if you hit it
prompt: SAMPLE: $20/mo × 10k possible customers is the ceiling. Burn is $25k/mo. If you actually hit that ceiling as revenue, how many months of burn does one month of ceiling cover?
hints: Ceiling = price × reachable customers.
Months of cover = ceiling ÷ monthly burn. Same shape as runway, with revenue instead of cash.
cheat: 20×10k = $200k ceiling. 200÷25 = 8 months of burn per month of ceiling. 200,000 is the ceiling dollars. 25,000 is burn. 0.125 inverted the ratio.

title: Lifetime months, then LTV
prompt: SAMPLE: 5% monthly churn, $20/mo price. About what LTV?
hints: Lifetime months ≈ 1 ÷ monthly churn.
LTV ≈ price × those months.
cheat: 1/0.05 = 20 months. 20×$20 = $400. 20 is the months, not the dollars. 100 is 5×20 (churn percent as a multiple). 240 is 12 months × $20.

title: Rule of 40, then burn multiple
prompt: SAMPLE: 30% growth, 15% margin, burn $2M, net new ARR $1M. Pick the pair: Rule of 40 sum, then burn multiple.
hints: Rule of 40 is growth % plus profit margin %.
Burn multiple is burn ÷ net new ARR.
cheat: 30+15=45 (passes ~40). 2÷1=2×. 30 forgot the margin. 0.5× inverted burn and ARR. 40 is the bar, not this company’s sum.

title: Payback months, then 3× smell
prompt: SAMPLE: CAC $240, $40/mo gross profit. Payback months, and what LTV do you need for a 3× CAC?
hints: Payback = CAC ÷ monthly gross profit. Aim ≤12.
3× CAC is the LTV smell. 3×$240.
cheat: 240÷40=6 months (inside ≤12). 3×240=$720 LTV. $240 is CAC, not LTV. 12 is the bar, not this payback. $80 is 2×$40 (two months of GP).

title: NRR 130, churn still 5%
prompt: SAMPLE: same-customer revenue $100k → $130k. Monthly logo churn is still 5%. What is NRR, and about how many lifetime months from that churn?
hints: NRR is later ÷ earlier on the same customers. New logos stay out.
Lifetime months ≈ 1 ÷ monthly churn. NRR can be >100% while logos still leave.
cheat: 130/100=130% NRR. 1/0.05≈20 months. 30% subtracted instead of the ratio. 5 months treated 5% as months. 80% would be a shrinking cohort.

title: Daily rate, then a year
prompt: SAMPLE: $30/day. Yearly cost if a month is 30 days?
hints: Monthly is daily ×30, not ×365.
Yearly is that monthly ×12. Same as ×360 days.
cheat: 30×30 = $900/mo. 900×12 = $10,800/year. 900 is still monthly. 360 is 30×12 without the daily dollars. 10,950 is 365×30.

title: 15% convert, then surplus
prompt: SAMPLE: 900 trial users, 15% pay. Ads plus tools are $3,000 and price is $50. Surplus customers after break-even?
hints: 15% is 10% plus 5%.
Break-even users = 3,000 ÷ 50. Surplus is payers minus that floor.
cheat: 10% of 900 = 90, 5% = 45 → 135 payers. 3,000 ÷ 50 = 60 to cover. Surplus 135 − 60 = 75. 60 stops at the break-even floor. 135 is the payers, not the surplus. 840 took 60 off all 900 trial users.

title: ÷5, then undo 1%
prompt: SAMPLE: 80 ÷ 5. That result is 1% of what number?
hints: ÷5 is ×2 then one place left.
1% is two places left, so undo 1% by appending two zeros.
cheat: 80×2=160, one place left → 16. 16 is 1% of 1,600. 16 is the quotient. 800 is the original. 160 forgot the last shift.

title: Left to right, then ×5
prompt: SAMPLE: 47 + 36, then multiply that sum by 5.
hints: Add tens, then ones: 40+30 and 7+6.
×5 is ×10 then half.
cheat: 70+13=83. 83×10=830, half → 415. 83 is the sum. 830 forgot to halve. 235 is 47×5.

title: 35², then scale
prompt: SAMPLE: you know 35² = 1,225. What is 350²?
hints: 35² is the near-ten glue: 3×4 and 25.
350 is 35 with one extra zero, so the square gets two extra zeros.
cheat: 35²=1,225. One extra zero on the factor → two on the square → 122,500. 12,250 is only one extra zero. 1,225 is 35². 3,500 is 35×100.

title: ARR smell, then lifetime months
prompt: SAMPLE: $80k MRR, 5% monthly logo churn. Pick the pair: ARR, then lifetime months.
hints: ARR is MRR ×12. $80k ×12 is a ~$1M smell, not $80k.
Lifetime months ≈ 1 ÷ monthly churn.
cheat: 80k×12=$960k ARR. 1/0.05=20 months. $80k forgot ×12. 5 months treated 5% as months. Exact $1M is the smell, not the product.

title: Fermi slice as a ceiling
prompt: SAMPLE: you can reach 1,000 buyers at $50/mo. Monthly ceiling for that slice?
hints: A slice is buyers × price, not the whole TAM.
Ceiling = price × reachable customers. Same multiply.
cheat: 1,000×$50 = $50k/mo. $600k would be 1,000×$600/year (a different Fermi). 1,000 is headcount. 50 is the price.

title: Percent sold, then a loaded hire
prompt: SAMPLE: $3M into $12M post. Then one $100k salary loaded ×1.3. Pick the pair.
hints: Percent sold = cash ÷ post-money.
Loaded cost is salary ×1.3, not the sticker salary.
cheat: 3/12=25% sold. 100×1.3=$130k loaded. 20% would be $2M into $10M. $100k is the sticker. 3% treated millions as a percent.

title: Nineteen-dollar seats for a year
prompt: SAMPLE: 42 seats at $19/mo. What is the yearly bill?
hints: ×19 is ×20 minus one copy.
Then ×12 is ×10 plus ×2.

title: Cartons under the cap
prompt: SAMPLE: 97 cartons of 94 units. The warehouse cap is 10,000 units. How many units of headroom are left?
hints: Distances from 100: −3 and −6. Cross subtract, multiply the gaps.
Then: what is missing to make 10,000?
cheat: 97 − 6 = 91, 3×6 = 18 → 9,118 units. 10,000 − 9,118 = 882. 9,118 is the total, not the headroom; 918 dropped the thousand; 1,118 subtracted the wrong way.

title: Square booth, daily rate
prompt: SAMPLE: A 43-ft square booth costs $0.10 per square foot per day. Daily cost?
hints: ×0.10 is one place left.
cheat: 1,600 + 240 + 9 = 1,849 sq ft. One place left → $184.90. $1,849 forgot the rate; $160.90 dropped the 2ab term (1,609).

title: Tables of seven
prompt: SAMPLE: 203 attendees, round tables of 7. How many full tables, with nobody left over?
hints: Trim for 7: drop the last digit, subtract twice it.
Then 7 × what = 203?
cheat: 20 − 2×3 = 14, a multiple of 7, so it splits. 7 × 29 = 203 → 29 tables. 30 rounds up for no reason; 28 leaves 7 people standing.

title: Team lunch, two days
prompt: SAMPLE: 48 people at $32 a lunch, for two days. Total?
hints: Partial products: 48 × 30 and 48 × 2.
Two days is one double.

title: Cube crate, nine shippers
prompt: SAMPLE: A 6-ft cube shipping crate is split evenly among 9 shippers. Cubic feet each?
hints: 6³ is a fact worth owning.
216 has digit sum 9, so it splits by 9.
cheat: 6³ = 216. Digit sum 9 → divisible by 9. 216 ÷ 9 = 24. 36 is 6²; 216 is the whole crate.

title: Register adds and a refund
prompt: SAMPLE: The register shows $47. Add an $8 item, then refund $6. New total?
cheat: 47 + 10 − 2 = 55. 55 − 10 + 4 = 49. $55 forgot the refund; $61 added the refund; $41 subtracted both.

title: Fifteen-dollar fee, then a discount
prompt: SAMPLE: 46 accounts pay a $15 setup fee. You waive 10%. What do you collect?
hints: ×15 is ×10 plus half of that.
10% is one place left; subtract it.

title: Check the invoice total
prompt: SAMPLE: Invoices of $4,738 and $2,595. A teammate says the total is $7,343. What does the digit-root check say?
hints: Digit root: add digits until one remains.
Roots of a sum add.
cheat: 4,738 → 4 and 2,595 → 3, so the sum must root to 7. 7,343 → 17 → 8. Reject. The true total is 7,333. A passing last digit does not save a failed root.

title: Break-even by partial quotients
prompt: SAMPLE: Monthly cost $936, price $24/mo. Users to break even?
hints: Users = cost ÷ price.
24 × 40 = 960 is one 24 too many.
cheat: 936 ÷ 24: 24 × 40 = 960, back off one → 39 users. 40 overshoots by $24; 24 is the price.

title: Restock at six dollars
prompt: SAMPLE: 1,346 parts at $6 each, worked with the Trachtenberg ×6 rule. The restock budget is $8,000. Over or under, and by how much?
hints: ×6 digit rule: digit + half the neighbor, +5 if the digit is odd. Right to left.
Then compare the total with 8,000.
cheat: 0 1346: 6 → 6; 4 → 4 + 3 = 7; 3 → 3 + 2 + 5 = 10 → 0, carry 1; 1 → 1 + 1 + 5 + 1 = 8 → $8,076. That is $76 over. $76 under flips the comparison; $924 under dropped the carry (7,076); $8,076 is the total, not the gap.

title: Logos are not boxes
prompt: SAMPLE: 1,200 customer logos. On a busy hour about 20% are on, and each box serves 30 at once. How many boxes?
hints: Concurrent first: busy is about 20% of logos.
Then boxes = simultaneous users ÷ per-box capacity.
cheat: 20% of 1,200 = 240 on at once. 240 ÷ 30 = 8 boxes. 40 sized for every logo at once. 4 used the quiet 10%. 240 is the concurrent count, not boxes.

title: Vendor max is not the plan
prompt: SAMPLE: 900 simultaneous users. The vendor says a box handles 50. Plan at a safe load. How many boxes?
hints: Safe load is about 70% of the advertised max.
Divide, then round up: a part box is a whole box.
cheat: Safe per box 0.7 × 50 = 35. 900 ÷ 35 ≈ 25.7 → 26 boxes. 18 trusted the vendor max. 25 rounded down and leaves users without a seat. 35 is the per-box plan, not the count.

title: Each box, make or lose?
prompt: SAMPLE: a $1.25/hr GPU holds 20 users on a $40/mo plan. Per box, per month, do you make or lose money, and how much?
hints: Put the box on a monthly clock: hourly × 720.
Contribution = price × users − box cost.
cheat: Box 1.25 × 720 = $900/mo. Revenue 40 × 20 = $800. 800 − 900 = −$100 a box. $775 subtracted the hourly price. +$100 flipped the sign. −$900 forgot the revenue.

title: Pad the burn, then runway
prompt: SAMPLE: $300k in the bank. The team guesses burn at $40k a month. Pad the guess, then about how many months of runway?
hints: A cost guess runs long: pad it ×1.3 once.
Runway = cash ÷ padded monthly burn.
cheat: Padded burn 40 × 1.3 = $52k. 300 ÷ 52 ≈ 5.8 months. 7.5 skipped the pad. 9.8 padded the cash instead of the burn. 4.4 padded twice (×1.7).

title: Mid-band funnel vs fixed costs
prompt: SAMPLE: 25,000 visits a month at a mid-band funnel (20% sign up, 5% of those pay). Price $60, fixed costs $12,000. Paid customers, and do they cover cost?
hints: Compress the funnel: 20% × 5% = 1% of visits.
Revenue = paid × price, then compare with fixed cost.
cheat: 1% of 25,000 = 250 paid. 250 × 60 = $15,000 against $12,000 → $3,000 spare. 5,000 stopped at signups. "$3,000 short" flipped the comparison. 1,250 applied 5% to visits.

title: Busy hour at a safe load
prompt: SAMPLE: 4,200 logos. About 20% are on at the busy hour. A GPU runs 20 jobs at max, and you plan at 70%. How many GPUs?
hints: Concurrent jobs: 20% of logos.
Safe jobs per GPU: 0.7 × max. Then divide.
cheat: 20% of 4,200 = 840 jobs. Safe per GPU 14. 840 ÷ 14 = 60 GPUs. 42 skipped the 70% plan. 210 sized every logo at max. 30 used the quiet 10%.

title: Cover the box, then fill it
prompt: SAMPLE: a $2/hr GPU, a $48/mo plan, and 40 users fit on a box. Users to cover the box, and monthly contribution when it is full?
hints: Box per month: hourly × 720.
Cover = box ÷ price. Full contribution = 40 × price − box.
cheat: Box 2 × 720 = $1,440. 1,440 ÷ 48 = 30 to cover. Full: 40 × 48 = $1,920 − 1,440 = +$480. The minus sign is backwards. 24 divided by $60. $1,920 is revenue before the box.

title: Give the heavy slice its own boxes
prompt: SAMPLE: 2,000 accounts. About 20% of them carry 80% of the load. The heavy accounts get dedicated boxes at 25 per box. How many boxes?
hints: The heavy slice is 20% of the accounts, not 80%.
Boxes = heavy accounts ÷ 25.
cheat: 20% of 2,000 = 400 heavy accounts. 400 ÷ 25 = 16 boxes. 80 boxed every account. 64 used the 80% (1,600) as a headcount. 20 is the percent, not the boxes.

title: Seats for a revenue goal
prompt: SAMPLE: the goal is $18,000 a month at $45 a seat. Seats needed, and yearly revenue at that goal?
hints: Users = revenue ÷ price. Cancel what you can.
Monthly × 12 for the year.
cheat: 18,000 ÷ 45 = 400 seats. 18,000 × 12 = $216,000 a year. 40 dropped a zero in the division. $21,600 dropped a zero in the ×12. 810 multiplied 18 × 45 instead of dividing.

title: Round the seats, pay back
prompt: SAMPLE: 49 seats at $38 a month. Monthly total?
hints: 49 is 50 − 1. Price 50 seats first.
Then pay back one $38 seat.
cheat: 50 × 38 = 1,900, minus one 38 → $1,862. $1,900 forgot the payback. $1,938 added it instead. $1,824 paid back two seats.

title: Two quotes near a square
prompt: SAMPLE: quote A is 62 × 58 units, quote B is 61 × 59 units. Which is larger, and by how much?
hints: Both pairs sit on 60. Each product is 60² minus the gap squared.
Compare the gaps: 2² against 1².
cheat: A = 3,600 − 4 = 3,596. B = 3,600 − 1 = 3,599. B is larger by 3. Same sums do not mean same products. "By 4" compared 2² with 0.

title: A refund without borrowing
prompt: SAMPLE: $5,003 in the account and a $1,998 vendor payment clears. Balance?
hints: Move both numbers the same way so the payment is round.
cheat: 5,005 − 2,000 = $3,005. $3,003 rounded only the payment. $3,001 took the 2 away instead of adding it. $3,105 is a borrowing slip.

title: Fraction of a fraction of a pool
prompt: SAMPLE: an advisor gets 3/8 of 4/9 of a 54,000-share pool. Shares?
hints: Cancel across before multiplying: 3 with 9, 4 with 8.
cheat: 1/6 of 54,000 = 9,000. 24,000 stopped at 4/9. 20,250 used only 3/8. 6,000 is 1/9 of the pool.

title: How long is the side?
prompt: SAMPLE: a square storage yard is 410 sq m. About how long is one side?
hints: Nearest square: 20² = 400, so d = 10.
Bump by d ÷ 2a = 10 ÷ 40.
cheat: 20 + 10/40 = 20.25 m (true ≈ 20.248). 20.5 bumped by d ÷ a. 21 rounded up to the next whole meter. 205 halved the area.

title: Pick the multiplication order
prompt: SAMPLE: 5 offices × 17 people × a $20 lunch stipend × 2 days. Total?
hints: Pair the round factors first: 5 × 20 × 2.
That is 200. Then × 17.
cheat: 5 × 20 × 2 = 200, × 17 = $3,400. $1,700 dropped the second day. $34,000 and $340 slipped a zero.

title: Three plates, a tip, six ways
prompt: SAMPLE: you and five colleagues order plates of $47, $38, and $65, then add a 20% tip. Even split per person?
hints: Add left to right: 40 + 30 + 60, then 7 + 8 + 5.
Tip: 10% doubled. Split by everyone at the table, you included.
cheat: Bill 150, tip 20% = 30 → 180, ÷ 6 = $30. $25 forgot the tip, $28.75 used a 15% habit, $36 split by 5 and left yourself out.

title: Resell a near-100 lot
prompt: SAMPLE: buy 98 units at $96, resell at 25% over cost, then give a bulk buyer 10% off. Revenue?
hints: Add a quarter, then take a tenth off what you have.
cheat: Cost 98 × 96 = 9,408. +25% (2,352) = 11,760, −10% (1,176) = $10,584. $10,819.20 netted the two as +15%, $11,760 forgot the discount, $10,800 rounded 98 to 100 and never paid it back.

title: Sod around a shed
prompt: SAMPLE: a 45 ft square lot with a 15 ft square shed on it. Sod costs $4 a sq ft. Cost to sod the rest?
hints: a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b), or square each: 45² ends in 25.
×4 is double, double.
cheat: 45² − 15² = 30 × 60 = 1,800 sq ft, ×4 = $7,200. $3,600 squared the difference of the sides (30²), $8,100 forgot to take out the shed, $9,000 added the shed instead.

title: Desks on an annual plan
prompt: SAMPLE: 11 desks at $46 a month, billed for the year with one month free, plus a $1,250 setup fee. First-year bill?
hints: ×11 is neighbor sums: 46 → 4 | 10 | 6, carry.
One month free means 11 billed months. Then add the setup.
cheat: 506 a month × 11 billed months = 5,566, + 1,250 = $6,816. $7,322 billed all 12 months, $5,566 forgot the setup, $6,072 did both.

title: Check the box count
prompt: SAMPLE: 4,236 widgets go into boxes of 12. A clerk’s sheet says 352 boxes. Right count?
hints: 12 = 4 × 3. 36 passes ÷4; digit sum 15 passes ÷3.
Check the sheet: 352 × 12 should land on 4,236.
cheat: 4,236 ÷ 4 = 1,059, ÷ 3 = 353. 352 trusts the sheet (352 × 12 = 4,224, digit root 3 vs 4,236’s 6). 363 split 3,600 + 636 and wrote 63 for 53. 1,059 stopped after ÷4.

title: Signups per page per week
prompt: SAMPLE: about 2,870 visitors a day spread over 41 landing pages, and 15% sign up. Signups per page in a week, roughly?
hints: Compatible numbers: 2,800 ÷ 40 = 70 a page a day.
A week is ×7; then 10% + 5%.
cheat: 2,870 ÷ 41 ≈ 2,800 ÷ 40 = 70, × 7 = 490, 15% = 73.5 → about 74. about 490 forgot the sign-up rate, about 7 used 1.5%, about 10 forgot the week.

title: Check the hotel folio
prompt: SAMPLE: 23 rooms at $41 a night for 3 nights. The folio says $2,839. True total?
hints: 23 × 41: ones 3, cross 2 + 12 = 14 → 4 carry 1, tens 8 + 1 = 9.
Then ×3, and check digit roots: 943 → 7, ×3 → 3.
cheat: 23 × 41 = 943, × 3 = $2,829 (digit root 3). $2,839 is the folio (root 4, so it is wrong), $2,760 dropped the ×1 cross and used 40, $943 is one night.

title: Till, then an invoice
prompt: SAMPLE: a $1,000 float takes in $47 and $38, refunds $26, then pays a $386 invoice. What is left?
hints: Then 1,059 − 386: count up from 386.
cheat: 1,000 + 47 + 38 − 26 = 1,059, − 386 = $673. $725 added the refund, $614 took the invoice off the float and ignored the till, $59 forgot the float.

title: Double, double, then tax the gain
prompt: SAMPLE: $40,000 grows at 9% a year for 16 years, then 37.5% of the gain goes to tax. What is left, roughly?
hints: 72 ÷ 9 = 8 years a doubling; 16 years is two.
37.5% = 3/8. Tax the gain, not the whole pot.
cheat: Two doublings: 40k → 160k, gain 120k, 3/8 of it = 45k → about $115,000. about $100,000 taxed the whole pot, about $45,000 is the tax, about $50,000 counted one doubling and taxed the whole pot.

title: Four hires, then the raise clock
prompt: SAMPLE: $1.8M in the bank, $98k a month of other net burn, and you add four engineers at $120k salary. Runway, and when do you start the raise?
hints: Load the salaries: 4 × 120k × 1.3, then ÷ 12.
Runway = cash ÷ net burn. A raise takes about six months.
cheat: 4 × 120k × 1.3 = 624k a year = 52k a month. Burn 150k → 1,800 ÷ 150 = 12 months; start the raise at 12 − 6 → 12 months — start the raise in 6. about 13 months — start in 7 left salaries unloaded, about 18 months — start in 12 forgot the hires, and 12 months — start the raise in 11 waits until the money is nearly gone.

title: Growth, NRR, and the 40 line
prompt: SAMPLE: MRR went from $250k to $300k this year, at a −15% margin. Last year’s customers alone now pay $270k a month. Rule of 40 score and NRR?
hints: Growth is (300 − 250) ÷ 250. The margin is negative.
NRR holds the customer list fixed: 270 ÷ 250.
cheat: Growth 50 ÷ 250 = 20%, + (−15) = 5. NRR 270 ÷ 250 = 108% → 5, NRR 108%. 35, NRR 108% dropped the minus, 5, NRR 120% put new logos into NRR (300 ÷ 250), 20, NRR 108% forgot the margin.

title: LTV to CAC from churn
prompt: SAMPLE: a $60/mo plan at 75% gross margin, 3% monthly churn, and a $450 CAC. LTV to CAC, roughly?
hints: Gross profit first: 75% of 60. Lifetime ≈ 1 ÷ 0.03.
LTV = GP × lifetime. Then divide by CAC.
cheat: GP $45 × about 33 months = $1,500 LTV, ÷ 450 = about 3.3×. about 4.4× used price instead of gross profit, about 1.2× counted only the first year, 10× is the payback in months (450 ÷ 45), not the ratio.

title: Take rate after card fees
prompt: SAMPLE: 20,000 orders a month at $30, a 12% take, and you pay 2.9% + $0.30 per order in card fees. Net revenue a month?
hints: Card fees run on every full charge: 2.9% of GMV plus 30¢ an order.
cheat: Take 12% of 600k = 72k. Fees 17.4k + 6k = 23.4k → $48,600. $54,600 forgot the 30¢ per order, $63,912 charged the 2.9% on revenue instead of GMV, $72,000 ignored fees.

title: TAM slice and the round
prompt: SAMPLE: 120k clinics at $50/mo. You raise $3M on a $12M pre-money to win 2% of that market. ARR target and percent sold?
hints: Yearly price first: $600. TAM = 120k × 600.
Post = pre + cash. Sold = cash ÷ post.
cheat: TAM $72M, 2% = $1.44M ARR; post $15M, 3 ÷ 15 = 20% → $1.44M ARR; 20% sold. $120k ARR; 20% sold used the monthly price, $1.44M ARR; 25% sold divided by pre, $14.4M ARR; 20% sold took 20% instead of 2%.

title: Busy hour to padded bill
prompt: SAMPLE: 3,000 logos, about 15% on at the busy hour. A box holds 50 users at max and you plan at 70%. Boxes cost $1.50/hr, and you pad the budget 30%. Monthly infra budget?
hints: 15% of 3,000 are on at once. Plan each box at 70% of 50.
Round boxes up. $1.50 × 720 a month, then pad once.
cheat: 450 active ÷ 35 safe = 12.9 → 13 boxes × $1,080 = 14,040, ×1.3 = $18,252. $12,636 planned at the 50-user max, $14,040 skipped the pad, $16,848 rounded 12.9 down to 12 boxes.

title: Ad spend to payback
prompt: SAMPLE: $60,000 of ads buys 40,000 visits. 20% sign up and 5% of signups pay $50/mo at an 80% gross margin. CAC payback in months?
hints: Paid = 40,000 × 20% × 5%. CAC = spend ÷ paid.
Payback divides CAC by gross profit, not price.
cheat: 400 paid → CAC $150; GP $40 → 3.75 months. 3 months divided by price, about 0.2 months treated every signup as a customer, 37.5 months used 0.5% instead of 5% (40 paid).

title: Quarter burn multiple
prompt: SAMPLE: this quarter you spent $2.4M, collected $0.9M, and MRR rose from $410k to $460k. Burn multiple, and how does it read?
hints: Net burn = spend − collections.
Net new ARR = the MRR change × 12.
cheat: Net burn 1.5M ÷ net new ARR (50k × 12 = 600k) → 2.5× — scaling, not efficient. 4× — expensive used gross spend, 30× — burning badly forgot to annualize the MRR change, 0.4× — very efficient flipped the ratio.

title: Boxes for the heavy accounts
prompt: SAMPLE: 400 accounts send 50,000 jobs a day and the top 20% send 80% of them. A box handles 2,000 jobs a day; plan at 70%. Boxes for the top accounts alone?
hints: Top 20% of accounts send 80% of 50,000 jobs.
Safe box = 70% of 2,000. Round up.
cheat: 40,000 heavy jobs ÷ 1,400 safe = 28.6 → 29. 20 planned at the 2,000 max, 28 rounded down, 8 sized the light 20% of jobs instead.
